title: ChatEED: An agentic retrieval assistant for accelerator operators
problem: Accelerator facility operators (SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory) manage critical operations via electronic logbooks (ELOGs) but face challenges: ELOG entries are time-consuming, complex, brief, incomplete, jargon-filled, and inconsistently structured. With thousands of records spanning decades, retrieving and interpreting critical information is difficult.
motivation: Accelerator operations depend on institutional knowledge captured in ELOGs, but poor information structure and manual search impede operator efficiency and knowledge transfer. Need for AI-assisted retrieval and summarization to improve shift continuity and communication.
method: ChatEED retrieves relevant entries from decades of electronic logbooks (ELOGs) and uses them to generate clear answers to operator questions, solving the problem that ELOG entries are often fragmented, jargon-heavy, and hard to search. To address operator needs, the system automatically summarizes shift reports, retrieves ELOG information in real-time as operators ask questions, and makes its reasoning transparent. It was built by interviewing accelerator facility operators and analyzing their actual workflows, which shaped its focus on security, efficiency, and modularity.
key_novelty: ChatEED brings human-centered design to AI-powered search for electronic logbooks by building the system directly from accelerator facility operators' workflows.
contributions: Agentic RAG system for ELOG retrieval and summarization
limitations: No quantitative metrics on retrieval accuracy or operator satisfaction
Scalability to other accelerator facilities not addressed
Integration with existing SLAC systems not detailed
Handling of sensitive/security-critical information not fully specified
